 Tulsi Vivah 2026: When is the sacred marriage? Check date, shubh muhurat, puja vidhi and significance
 Tulsi Vivah 2026 will be celebrated on November 21, marking the ceremonial marriage of Goddess Tulsi to Lord Vishnu. The festival signifies the end of Chaturmas and the beginning of the Hindu wedding season. 
 MC Lifestyle Desk 
 November 16, 2026 / 14:43 IST 
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Tulsi Vivah 2026 will be celebrated on November 21. 
 Tulsi Vivah, an important festival in the Hindu calendar, will be observed on Saturday, November 21, 2026. The occasion celebrates the symbolic marriage of Goddess Tulsi to Lord Vishnu, who is represented by the sacred Shaligram stone. Devotees decorate Tulsi plants as brides and perform traditional wedding rituals to mark the divine union.
 The festival falls on Kartik Shukla Dwadashi, the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of the Hindu month of Kartik. It is observed after Dev Uthani Ekadashi, when Lord Vishnu is believed to awaken from his four-month-long cosmic rest. 
 Tulsi Vivah 2026: Date and Shubh Muhurat
According to Drik Panchang, Tulsi Vivah will be celebrated on November 21. The Dwadashi Tithi will begin at 6:31 am on November 21 and end at 4:56 am on November 22. 
 The ceremony is traditionally performed during Godhuli Vela, the evening twilight period. However, the exact auspicious timing can vary depending on the location and regional customs. 
 Why is Tulsi Vivah celebrated?
Tulsi Vivah commemorates the marriage of Goddess Tulsi and Lord Vishnu. The festival holds religious significance as it marks the conclusion of Chaturmas, a four-month period during which many Hindu communities avoid auspicious ceremonies such as weddings.
 Devotees believe that performing Tulsi Vivah brings prosperity, happiness and marital harmony. The occasion also marks the beginning of the Hindu wedding season. 
 The story of Vrinda and Lord Vishnu
According to Hindu mythology, Tulsi was originally Vrinda, the devoted wife of demon king Jalandhar. Her devotion and chastity were believed to protect her husband, making him nearly invincible.
 To defeat Jalandhar, Lord Vishnu assumed his appearance and deceived Vrinda. When she discovered the truth, she cursed Vishnu to turn into stone. The curse is associated with the origin of Shaligram worship.

 Lord Vishnu later blessed Vrinda, declaring that she would be worshipped as the sacred Tulsi plant and remain dear to him. Their divine marriage is commemorated through Tulsi Vivah. 
 Tulsi Vivah 2026: Puja Vidhi and Rituals
Devotees begin by cleaning and decorating the Tulsi plant and the surrounding area. The plant is dressed in a red chunari, flowers and traditional ornaments, while a Shaligram stone or Vishnu idol is decorated as the groom.
 A small wedding mandap is often prepared using sugarcane stalks. Devotees offer flowers, fruits, sweets, haldi, kumkum, rice and diyas during the puja.
 The ceremony includes prayers to Lord Ganesha, symbolic Kanyadaan, exchange of garlands and wedding rituals such as pheras, depending on family traditions. The celebrations conclude with aarti and distribution of prasad. 
 What is the significance of Shaligram?
Shaligram is a sacred black stone regarded as a representation of Lord Vishnu. It is traditionally worshipped alongside Tulsi, whose leaves are considered especially sacred in Vishnu worship. 
 The ceremonial marriage of Tulsi and Shaligram symbolises their eternal divine bond and reminds devotees of the importance of faith and devotion.
